_about: Field-sample to lab-comparison activity (Prompt 08, Part S). Read by ScienceActions. Every mineral share here is ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT FROM THE ARCHIVE: the source register (docs/source_register.md, S06) gives only the mission, instrument, site and data set of the reference, and that CheMin measures mineral abundance by X-ray diffraction of powdered rock and soil. Which rock lies at which site on the map is made up for the game. A Gale crater value is never a measurement of the fictional map.

groups.name: Volcanic minerals
groups.detail: feldspar, pyroxene and olivine crystals, found in dark volcanic rock

groups.name: Clay minerals
groups.detail: very fine minerals that usually form when water changes rock

groups.name: Sulfate salts
groups.detail: salty minerals such as gypsum, left behind when salty water dries

groups.name: Glassy material
groups.detail: material with no crystal pattern, so X-rays show no clear peaks

control.name: Empty sample holder (blank control)
control.why: The same measurement with nothing in the holder. It shows what the machine reads by itself, so you know the signal comes from the sample and not from the instrument.

interpretations.text: Mostly volcanic minerals, like reference 1: dark volcanic sand or rock.
Much more clay than reference 1: this rock was changed by water long ago.
Much more sulfate salt than reference 1: a salty crust left by drying water.

volcanic.name: dark volcanic sand
volcanic.use: It adds little plant food, so a bed mixed with it needs a higher nutrient setting.

clay.name: clay-rich soil
clay.use: Clay holds on to plant food, so a bed mixed with it needs a middle nutrient setting.

sulfate.name: salty sulfate crust
sulfate.use: It is salty, so a bed mixed with it needs a lower nutrient setting to keep the mix from getting too salty.

use_note: In this game the greenhouse planter mix contains some crushed local ground, so the lab result suggests a nutrient setting. This is made up for the game: growing crops in Mars ground has not been shown.
